question: In covering a distance of 52 km, Anmol takes 6 hours more than Nikhil. If Anmol doubles his speed, then he would take 7 hours less than Nikhil. Anmol's speed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **Anmol** doubles his **speed** (Ratio 1 : 2), his **time** ratio becomes 2 : 1.

The difference in time units = 2 − 1 = 1 unit.

Actual time difference = 6 hours (late) + 7 hours (early) = 13 hours.

Original time taken by **Anmol** = 2 units = 2 × 13 = 26 hours.

**Anmol** speed = Distance ÷ Original Time = 52 ÷ 26 = 2 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a12cfc93d31a2780204ea081aa60b0a577d65d305cae9f3db65da5a2d2c3f7d.png] 

**Given:** Total distance = 52 km. Let **Anmol** original speed be s km/hr.

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Original time (T₁) = 52 ÷ s

⇒ New time (T₂) = 52 ÷ 2s

⇒ Time difference = T₁ − T₂ = (Nikhil + 6) − (Nikhil − 7) = 13 hours

⇒ (52 ÷ s) − (52 ÷ 2s) = 13

⇒ (104 − 52) ÷ 2s = 13

⇒ 52 ÷ 2s = 13

⇒ 26 ÷ s = 13

⇒ s = 26 ÷ 13 = 2 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

For a constant **distance**, **speed** is inversely proportional to **time** (S ∝ 1/T). If speed is doubled, time is halved.

Time Difference Concept

When one case is **late** and the other is **early**, the total time difference is the sum of both values (x late + y early = x + y difference).

Average Speed Formula

If a person covers equal distances at speeds **u** and **v**, the **Average Speed** = 2uv ÷ (u + v).</p
